note: Track dim-aug, step 1: the diminished triad, 1 ♭3 ♭5, built on two staffs against the minor triad, heard whole on the chord boxes and checked in the ear game ("qualities": min and dim, named as its buttons show them), then found on the 7th note of a major key, named as chord tokens counted the long way. The root is fixed (no moves), and each section has a feel to reach.

exercise.title: The diminished triad
exercise.why: A diminished triad is a minor triad with the 5th lowered a half step, so listening for that one note tells the two chords apart.

cells.text: Tap {{1}}, {{b3}} and {{5}} on the staff below: C minor, one note at a time.

Now tap {{1}}, {{b3}} and the ringed {{b5}} on this staff: C diminished. Only the top note moved, down a half step.
Practice until you can hum the lowered note before you tap it.
Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Go from Cm to Cdim and back, and listen for the one note that drops.

Then press Start in the game below: it plays a minor or a diminished triad from any root, and you pick Minor or Diminished.
Practice until you can tell them apart before the chord has faded.

The panel below shows the chord on every note of C major. Press each chord in turn: {{chord:vii°}}, the 7th chord of the key, built on {{7}}, is the only diminished one.
Then press {{chord:vii°}} and {{chord:I}}, the 1st chord, after it, and listen for the diminished chord leading home.
Practice until you can hum the home note as soon as {{chord:vii°}} sounds.
